Class Bits

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.util.Bits
public final class Bits extends Object
A compact collection of static utilities for manipulating bit masks stored in a 64-bit long. This class provides common operations such as checking, setting, clearing, toggling individual bits or masks, identifying the positions of the first or highest set bit, counting bits, and constraining a mask to a fixed width.

All operations treat bit index 0 as the least significant bit (LSB) of the 64-bit word and bit index 63 as the most significant bit. Since long is inherently unsigned in its bit representation, all operations use Java’s standard two's-complement bitwise semantics.

This class is final with a private constructor because it is intended purely as a static utility library.

    • firstSet

      public static int firstSet(long bits)
      Returns the index (0-based) of the lowest set bit (LSB-first). That is, it returns the position of the first bit whose value is 1.

      This method is equivalent to Long.numberOfTrailingZeros(long) when bits != 0.

      Parameters:
      bits - the 64-bit word
      Returns:
      index of the lowest set bit, or -1 if bits == 0

    • highestSet

      public static int highestSet(long bits)
      Returns the index (0-based) of the highest set bit (MSB-first). That is, it returns the position of the most significant bit whose value is 1.

      This method is equivalent to: 

      63 - Long.numberOfLeadingZeros(bits)
      Parameters:
      bits - the 64-bit word
      Returns:
      index of the highest set bit, or -1 if bits == 0

      public static long unsetAll()

    • mask

      public static long mask(long bits, int width)
      Returns the value of bits truncated to a field of width width bits (from the least significant side).

      If width <= 0, the method returns 0L. If width >= 64, the method returns bits unchanged.

      Internally this method constructs a low-order mask of the form (1L << width) - 1 and applies it with bitwise AND.

      Parameters:
      bits - the original value
      width - number of low bits to preserve (range 1–64)
      Returns:
      the masked value
